alt.en: Part of an old printed page: the heading "ARTICLE VII." and the italic title "Dedication and Release.", then Section 1, "Dedication and consecration of persons, property and service", Section 2, "Dedication and release of private claim", and a closing paragraph dated November 1831, in plain type.
alt.es: Parte de una página impresa antigua: el encabezado "ARTICLE VII." y el título en cursiva "Dedication and Release.", luego la sección 1, "Dedication and consecration of persons, property and service", la sección 2, "Dedication and release of private claim", y un párrafo final fechado en noviembre de 1831, en tipos sencillos.

caption.en: Article VII of the covenant of the Shaker Church at Harvard, Massachusetts (not this song's village), dated 16 November 1831 and printed in 1873, by which its members "give up ourselves and services together with all our temporal interest": Church members gave their own property to the community, and songs like this one promised the faithful a treasure in heaven.
caption.es: El artículo VII del pacto de la Iglesia shaker de Harvard, Massachusetts (no es la aldea de esta canción), fechado el 16 de noviembre de 1831 e impreso en 1873, por el que sus miembros prometen "give up ourselves and services together with all our temporal interest" (entregarnos a nosotros mismos y nuestros servicios, junto con todos nuestros bienes temporales): los miembros de la Iglesia entregaban sus propios bienes a la comunidad, y canciones como esta prometían a los fieles un tesoro en el cielo.

source: Roxalana L. Grosvenor, The Shakers' Covenant, (Never before Published,) with a Brief Outline of Shaker History (Boston: W. C. Allan, Printer, 1873), p. 8: the "Covenant or Constitution" of the Church of the United Society in the town of Harvard, Mass., Article VII, "Dedication and Release" (cropped to Article VII; the end of Article VI above it is left out)
library: Boston Public Library (scan on the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed in Boston in 1873 ("Entered According to Act of Congress April 16, 1873, by Roxalana L. Grosvenor"); the crop shows only the covenant of the Church of the United Society at Harvard, Mass., an unsigned corporate text dated 16 November 1831, and no words by Grosvenor (born 1813, Library of Congress name authority n94093499; death year not found). Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70; anonymous works 70 years from publication, here 1873) and Mexico (life plus 100: the 1831 covenant's makers, adult Shakers in 1831, all died before 1926). Scan of a flat page.
credit: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Part of an old printed page: the heading "HYMN XXVI.", the italic title "The true Believer's Treasure.", and the hymn's first verse and the start of its second, in worn type.
alt.es: Parte de una página impresa antigua: el encabezado "HYMN XXVI.", el título en cursiva "The true Believer's Treasure." y la primera estrofa del himno y el comienzo de la segunda, en tipos gastados.

caption.en: Not this song but an older Shaker hymn, "The true Believer's Treasure", in Millennial Praises (Hancock, Massachusetts, 1813): its treasure is "safe from moth and rust", from the same saying of Jesus that O the Beautiful Treasure echoes.
caption.es: No es esta canción, sino un himno shaker más antiguo, "The true Believer's Treasure" (el tesoro del verdadero creyente), de Millennial Praises (Hancock, Massachusetts, 1813): su tesoro está "safe from moth and rust" (a salvo de la polilla y el óxido), el mismo dicho de Jesús del que se hace eco O the Beautiful Treasure.

source: Millennial Praises, Containing a Collection of Gospel Hymns, in Four Parts (Hancock, Mass.: Printed by Josiah Tallcott, Junior, 1813), compiled by Seth Youngs Wells, Part II, Hymn XXVI, "The true Believer's Treasure", p. 199 (lower half)
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (scan on the Internet Archive)
callNumber: SCB; Internet Archive millennialpraise00well, leaf n212 (p. 199)
licenceEvidence: Printed 1813; compiler Seth Youngs Wells died 1847; the hymns are unsigned. Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70; anonymous works 70 years from publication) and Mexico (life plus 100: Wells died 1847; any 1813 hymn writer died long before 1926). Scan of a flat page.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive
